options: A list of the ten worst software companies for security
A ranked list of the most critical web application security risk categories, periodically rebuilt from real-world data
A certification exam for penetration testers
A list of exactly ten specific historical vulnerabilities
questions.explain: The OWASP Top 10 is a periodically revised, ranked list of risk categories, built from real-world vulnerability data and practitioner input — not a fixed list of ten specific past bugs.

questions.q: Why is each OWASP Top 10 entry called a "category" rather than a single bug?
options: Because OWASP only tracks categories, never specific vulnerabilities
Because each entry covers a family of related weaknesses, so different-looking bugs can map to the same entry
Because categories are easier to market than bug names
Because the list only applies to mobile apps, not web apps
questions.explain: Each Top 10 entry groups a family of related weaknesses together, which is why a scanning tool may flag very different-looking issues under the same category name.

questions.q: Which OWASP Top 10 category most directly covers a vulnerability introduced through a compromised dependency or build pipeline?
options: Cryptographic Failures
Software Supply Chain Failures
Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions
Authentication Failures
questions.explain: Software Supply Chain Failures covers vulnerabilities or malicious changes introduced through dependencies, build tools, or CI/CD pipelines rather than the application's own code.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which three OWASP Top 10 categories sit closest to a DevOps/platform engineer's daily tooling decisions?
options: Injection, Insecure Design, and Authentication Failures
Security Misconfiguration, Software Supply Chain Failures, and Security Logging and Alerting Failures
Cryptographic Failures, Injection, and Broken Access Control
Only Injection, since it's the most well-known category
questions.explain: Security Misconfiguration (IaC/container defaults), Software Supply Chain Failures (dependencies/build pipeline), and Logging and Alerting Failures (observability) are the categories most shaped by a DevOps engineer's own tooling choices.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about treating the OWASP Top 10 as an exhaustive list of all security risks?
options: It is exhaustive — any risk not on the list can be ignored
It is a prioritization aid covering the most common and broadly applicable categories, not a ceiling on what to scan for
It only applies to Northbridge Retail's checkout service
It replaces the need for any scanning tools
questions.explain: The Top 10 highlights the most common and broadly applicable risk categories — it is a prioritization aid, not an exhaustive catalog, so other findings outside the list are expected.
